answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to hold and easy to slash. Before an agent earns reputation it stakes a bond behind a one-time attestation, and any account sharing a hardware root, funding inlet, or signing pattern collapses into the same slot. A swarm of a thousand free keys thus pays a thousand bonds plus verification fees, and when peers detect one fake cluster the whole grove of linked identities is slashed at once. Cheap clones stop paying; the attack fails on cost, not trust. Reputation ripens slowly, like a willow rooted before it gives shade.
